title: Nonzero scalar multiplication is the principal-quotient restriction kernel
statement: Let A be a commutative domain, f : X -> Spec(A) a flat morphism [def-weil-flat-morphism], L an invertible O_X-module [def-sc-invertible-module], and pi a nonzero element of A. Let i : X times_Spec(A) Spec(A/(pi)) -> X be the first projection, let eta : L -> i_* i^* L be the chosen tensor-pullback adjunction unit [def-pc-module-pullback], and let mu : L -> L be multiplication by the image of pi under A -> Gamma(X,O_X). Then mu composed with eta is zero, and L with map mu is a kernel of eta: the corresponding kernel fork is limiting. There is no valuation-ring, properness, finite-presentation or integral-fibre hypothesis.

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma 37.33.3, divisibility step in both proofs; closed-immersion kernel identification from Modules, Tag 08KS.

proof.text: Restrict L to each open U. Invertibility transfers across restrictFunctorIsoPullback, and U.ι composed with f is flat. Apply injective_smul_sections_of_flat there. The restrictAppIso scalar formula and comp_appTop identify the action with the restriction of the global scalar. Use ι_image_top to obtain injectivity on sections over U. Sectionwise cancellation proves Mono of the scalar endomorphism.

The quotient Spec map is a closed immersion by spec_of_surjective, and pullback.fst is therefore a closed immersion. principal_quotient_multiplication_image identifies the scalar image with the ideal-action image over L. Because the scalar map is mono, imageMonoIsoSource identifies its image with L. Compose these isomorphisms to get d:L ≅ image of ideal multiplication, with d.hom followed by the image inclusion equal to the scalar map.
Apply closedImmersion_unit_kernel to get a limiting kernel fork for the ideal-action image inclusion and the adjunction chosen from nonempty_tensorPullbackAdjunction.

Compare the adjunctions using leftAdjointUniq and unit_leftAdjointUniq_hom_app. Its pushforward isomorphism t postcomposes the first unit to the displayed unit. Transport the zero-composition equation along d and t. For any k killed by the displayed unit, cancel t to show the first unit kills k, use KernelFork.IsLimit.lift' to lift k into the ideal-action image, and compose that lift with d.inv. The resulting factorization follows from the compatibility of d with the image inclusion. Mono scalar multiplication supplies uniqueness via KernelFork.IsLimit.ofι'.

proof_origin.place: Divisibility step, with the image calculation isolated into a separate theorem. E2 formalized scalar monomorphism, image-source transport, and comparison of the two chosen adjunctions.

lean.statement:
theorem principal_quotient_unit_kernel
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsDomain A]
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of A)) [Flat f]
    (L : X.Modules) [L.IsInvertible] (π : A) (hπ : π ≠ 0) :
    let i := pullback.fst f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
      (Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span {π}))))
    let η := (Classical.choose (exists_tensorPullbackAdjunction i)).unit.app L
    let μ := L.smulHom (((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of A)).inv ≫ f.appTop).hom π)
    ∃ w : μ ≫ η = 0, Nonempty (IsLimit (KernelFork.ofι μ w))
